title: Logic design
summary: The design flow, RTL to gates, timing, power and verification coverage.

ideas.how: RTL describes what a circuit does; tools work out the gates
verification takes more effort than writing the design

learn.plain: Designing a chip is like writing a huge program that turns into a city plan. Engineers write code that describes circuits, software turns it into billions of tiny switches, and checking that everything works takes longer than writing it. Every choice trades speed, power and size against each other.
learn.engineer: Static timing analysis checks setup and hold on every path across process, voltage and temperature corners with on-chip variation derates. Power sign-off covers dynamic power (αCV²f), leakage and IR drop, managed with clock gating, multiple voltage domains and dynamic voltage and frequency scaling. Verification combines UVM constrained-random simulation, formal property checking and hardware emulation, tracked by code and functional coverage.

options: Code describing what registers and logic do each clock cycle
quiz.why: Register-transfer level code, written in languages such as SystemVerilog, is what synthesis turns into gates.

quiz.q: What sets a chip's maximum clock speed?
options: The slowest logic path between flip-flops (the critical path)
quiz.why: Every path must settle within one clock period. Pipeline registers shorten the critical path.

quiz.q: Why does raising the clock frequency increase power much faster than speed?
options: Higher frequency needs higher voltage, and dynamic power grows with voltage squared
It doesn't: power grows exactly in step with speed
quiz.why: P = α·C·V²·f. Raising f also requires raising V, so power climbs steeply.
